## Definition of Delay

**Arrival Time Variance (minutes)**  
Actual Arrival − Scheduled Arrival

**Thresholds**
- **Delayed:** > 5 minutes  
- **Excessively delayed:** > 10 minutes  

**Rationale**
- Based on NYC Ferry operational definitions  
- Chosen for technical feasibility (stable classification, less noise)

```{.r .cell-code}
trip_2025 <- read.csv("E:/MUSA/8010 practicum/data-selected/NYCF_data_compiled/trip_data/NYCF_trip_data_2025.01_06.csv")

trip_2024 <- trip_2024 %>% janitor::clean_names()
trip_2025 <- trip_2025 %>% janitor::clean_names()

make_logical_match <- function(df) {
  match_cols <- names(df)[str_detect(names(df), "match")]
  
  df %>%
    mutate(across(all_of(match_cols), ~ case_when(
      .x %in% c(TRUE, "TRUE", "True", "true", "T", "1", 1) ~ TRUE,
      .x %in% c(FALSE, "FALSE", "False", "false", "F", "0", 0) ~ FALSE,
      TRUE ~ NA
    )))
}

trip_2024 <- make_logical_match(trip_2024)
trip_2025 <- make_logical_match(trip_2025)


trip <- bind_rows(trip_2024, trip_2025)
```

```{.r .cell-code}
parse_dt_nycf <- function(x, tz_local) {
  x_chr <- as.character(x)
  x_chr <- str_trim(na_if(x_chr, ""))

  has_ampm <- str_detect(x_chr, regex("\\b(am|pm)\\b", ignore_case = TRUE))
  has_ampm[is.na(has_ampm)] <- FALSE

  out <- as.POSIXct(rep(NA, length(x_chr)), tz = tz_local)

  idx_2024 <- !has_ampm & !is.na(x_chr)
  idx_2025 <-  has_ampm & !is.na(x_chr)

  out[idx_2024] <- mdy_hm(x_chr[idx_2024], tz = tz_local, quiet = TRUE)
  out[idx_2025] <- parse_date_time(x_chr[idx_2025], orders = "mdY IMSp", tz = tz_local, quiet = TRUE)

  out
}

tz_local <- "America/New_York"

trip2 <- trip %>%
  mutate(
    scheduled_departure_dt = parse_dt_nycf(scheduled_departure_dt, tz_local),
    actual_departure_dt    = parse_dt_nycf(actual_departure_dt, tz_local),
    scheduled_arrival_dt   = parse_dt_nycf(scheduled_arrival_dt, tz_local),
    actual_arrival_dt      = parse_dt_nycf(actual_arrival_dt, tz_local),

    arr_diff_min = as.numeric(difftime(actual_arrival_dt, scheduled_arrival_dt, units = "mins")),

    delay_5  = arr_diff_min > 5,
    delay_10 = arr_diff_min > 10,  # excessive delay（可选）
    month    = floor_date(mdy(trip_date), "month"),
    hour     = hour(scheduled_departure_dt),
    day_type = workday
  )
```
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
route_order <- trip2 %>%
  group_by(route_no) %>%
  summarise(mean_delay = mean(delay_5, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(mean_delay) %>%
  pull(route_no)

trip2 <- trip2 %>%
  mutate(route_no = factor(route_no, levels = route_order))

trip2 %>%
  group_by(route_no, day_type) %>%
  summarise(delay_rate = mean(delay_5, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = route_no, y = delay_rate, fill = day_type)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7, alpha = 0.9) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Weekday" = "#F8766D", "Weekend" = "#00BFC4")) +
  theme_gray() +
  labs(
    title = "Delay Rate (>5 min) by Route",
    subtitle = "Weekday vs Weekend",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Share of trips delayed",
    fill = NULL
  )
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Trip_data_EDA_files/figure-html/p-route-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::



There is structural variation across routes.
The Rockaway route (RW) shows the highest delay rates, particularly on weekends where it exceeds 30%.
This suggests capacity or demand-driven congestion on leisure-heavy routes.”


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
trip2 %>%
  group_by(month, day_type) %>%
  summarise(delay_rate = mean(delay_5, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=month, y=delay_rate, color=day_type)) +
  geom_line(size=1) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels=scales::percent_format()) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks="1 month", date_labels="%Y-%m") +
  labs(
    title="Delay Rate (>5 min) by Month",
    x=NULL,
    y="Share delayed",
    color=NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle=45, hjust=1))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Trip_data_EDA_files/figure-html/p-month-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::

Delay rates exhibit strong seasonality.
We see a clear summer spike in 2024, particularly during weekends, where delay rates exceed 20%.This pattern likely reflects increased seasonal demand and recreational travel.Winter months show relatively improved reliability

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
trip2 %>%
  group_by(hour, day_type) %>%
  summarise(delay_rate = mean(delay_5, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=hour, y=delay_rate, color=day_type)) +
  geom_line(size=1) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=0:23) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels=scales::percent_format()) +
  labs(
    title="Delay Rate (>5 min) by Departure Hour",
    x="Hour of Day",
    y="Share delayed",
    color=NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Trip_data_EDA_files/figure-html/p-hour-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::

Delay rates peak in the mid-afternoon between 2pm and 5pm, particularly on weekends.Unlike typical commuter systems, the delay peak is not concentrated in the morning rush hour, but rather in mid-day leisure travel periods.

Taken together, these patterns suggest that delay is driven less by commuter peaks and more by high-demand recreational periods, particularly on routes serving waterfront leisure destinations
